Pages as folders of `app/`, like Next.js' App Router: `page.py`, `layout.py`, `template.py`,
`loading.py`, `error.py`, `not_found.py`, `[id]`, `[...slug]`, `[[...slug]]` and `(group)`.
See the [routing guide](/pyzed/guides/routing/).

```python
pz.run(pz.RouterApp("app", title="Shop"))
```

## The router

### `RouterApp`

```python
class RouterApp
```

An app whose window shows its routes:

```python
pz.run(pz.RouterApp("app", title="Shop"))

class Shop(pz.RouterApp):           # or subclass it
    routes = "app"
    title = "Shop"
    size = (1100, 720)
```

The window's title follows the page (its `title` or `metadata`, with the root layout's
`title_template`); the app's own `title` is used when the page has none. Alt+Left/Right,
the mouse's back and forward buttons and Android's back button move in the history.
`on_navigate(location)` runs after every navigation.

```python
class Shop(pz.RouterApp):
routes = "app"
title = "Shop"
```

### `Router`

```python
class Router
```

Routes in folders, like Next.js' App Router, or in a dict; see `pyzed.routing`.

`routes` is the `app/` folder (a relative path is looked for next to the file that creates the
router, then in the current folder), or a dict such as `{"/": home, "/users/[id]": user}`.
`initial` is the first location and `stale_time` how many seconds the data of a page stays
fresh: after that, going to it again (not back or forward) loads it again.

```python
self.router = pz.Router("app")
# in view(): return self.router.view()
```

## Links and hooks

### `link`

```python
link(href, content=None, *, replace=False, prefetch=True, router=None, size=None)
```

A link to `href` (`<Link>` in Next.js): text in the accent color, or any widget, that navigates
when clicked.

`href` is a path (`"/products/3"`), relative to the current page (`"../"`, `"reviews"`), a
query (`"?page=2"`) or `("/users/[id]", {"id": 7})`. `replace` replaces the history entry
instead of adding one; `prefetch` starts the page's `load` when the mouse is over the link.

```python
pz.link("/products/3", "See the monitor")
```

### `nav_link`

```python
nav_link(href, label, *, icon=None, exact=None, router=None, description=None)
```

A row for a sidebar or a menu (`ui.list_item`) that goes to `href` and shows as selected while
that page, or a page under it, is open (`exact=True`: only that page; the root `/` is exact).

```python
pz.nav_link("/settings", "Settings", icon="settings")
```

### `use_router`

```python
use_router()
```

The router drawing this view (`useRouter()`): `use_router().push("/cart")`.

Outside a view (a callback, a form's handler) it is the router that drew last.

```python
pz.use_router().push("/cart")
```

### `use_pathname`

```python
use_pathname()
```

The current path, like `/products/3` (`usePathname()`).

### `use_params`

```python
use_params()
```

The parameters of the current page: `{"id": "3"}` for `/products/[id]` (`useParams()`).

### `use_search_params`

```python
use_search_params()
```

The current query as a dict, `get_all(key)` for repeated keys (`useSearchParams()`).

## Inside pages

### `not_found`

```python
not_found()
```

Stops drawing the page (or its `load`) and shows the closest `not_found` file, like Next.js'
`notFound()`:

```python
async def load(params):
    product = await shop.get(params["id"])
    if product is None:
        pz.not_found()
    return product
```

### `redirect`

```python
redirect(href, *, push=False)
```

Goes to `href` instead of the page being drawn (from a page, a layout or a `load`).

The current history entry is replaced, like Next.js' `redirect()`; `push=True` adds one.

```python
pz.redirect("/login")
```

### `Location`

```python
@dataclass
class Location(pathname='/', search='', hash='')
```

Where the router is: `pathname` (`/products/3`), the `search` query without `?` and the
`hash` without `#`. The same parts as a browser's URL, so a route maps to a web address as is.

### `SearchParams`

```python
class SearchParams
```

The query of the URL (`?tab=reviews&tag=a&tag=b`) as a dict of the first values.

`get_all("tag")` gives every value of a repeated key, `str()` the encoded query.
